title: Learning: Who Built This?
text: The build system publishes an artifact to the registry, and the deployer pulls it. Each can check where it came from.
held: The artifact carried a signed account of its origin, and both hops read it.

cards.label: Reject the upload
cards.why: Nothing was wrong with it. Refusing something legitimate without looking is its own failure: check, then act.

fields.label: provenance
fields.value: built by the pipeline from commit 4be1f0a
fields.ok: Signed by the build system: built from commit 4be1f0a (tag v2.4.0).

intrusion.detail: No attestation. Nothing says where this artifact came from.
intrusion.why: An artifact with no provenance could have been built anywhere, by anyone who can upload.
intrusion.reveal: The artifact arrived at the Registry with no provenance attached.

temptations.label: Publish now and attach the provenance later
temptations.why: Later never checks anything. Once it is published, others pull it; the account of its origin has to arrive with it.

cards.label: Refuse to deploy
cards.why: Nothing was wrong with it. Refusing something legitimate without looking is its own failure: check, then act.

fields.label: policy
fields.value: only artifacts built by the pipeline from main

fields.label: digest
fields.check: Compare the digest with the provenance
fields.ok: The digest matches what the build system signed.

intrusion.value: sha256:d00d… (not the one in the provenance)
intrusion.detail: The digest differs from the one the build system signed.
intrusion.why: The name was right and the bytes were not. This is a different artifact wearing the same label.
intrusion.reveal: The artifact served to the Deployer was not the one the build produced.

temptations.label: Deploy to production first and verify afterwards
temptations.why: Verifying after it runs is finding out, not preventing. The gate is before production or it isn't a gate.

teaches: Provenance is a signed statement from the builder: this artifact, from this commit, by this pipeline.
A digest ties the name to exact bytes. Compare it with what was signed.
A check after deployment is a report, not a control.
